title: Capacity guardrails & project key patterns — demo with Sierra Health
next_steps: Send tailored pricing matrix and dedicated capacity options
Schedule proof-of-concept kickoff for week of Sep 8
action_items: Jordan Liu - Send pricing matrix and dedicated options - 2025-09-02
Priya Nair - Prep POC runbook and sample configs - 2025-09-05
Marta Ruiz - Confirm internal POC stakeholders and test scenarios - 2025-09-03
summary: Demo focused on multi-tenant rate limits, org vs project keys, and capacity guardrails for clinical inference workloads. Customer cares about per-tenant burst, SLA for patient-facing latency, and strict audit logs. Demo walked through Console policies, API keys, fairshare routing and suggested POC with dedicated capacity and KV cache settings.
transcript:
Header: 2025-08-28 15:00 UTC; Duration 20 minutes; Attendees: Jordan Liu (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Sierra Health - Head of AI), Ben Carter (Sierra Health - Platform Eng), Lena Ortiz (Sierra Health - Security).
00:00 Jordan Liu: hey everyone thanks for taking the time today. you should all have the deck link in chat, i'll do a quick agenda then priya will jump in with the console demo.
00:12 Marta Ruiz: thanks, jordan. quick context, we run inference for patient triage and expected latency is under 250ms p50, we also have strict PHI rules so data residency and auditability are non negotiable.
00:30 Priya Nair: got it. we usually see those as the main tradeoffs — latency vs cost and isolation. i'll show how org vs project keys map to tenant isolation, and how guardrails enforce burst/bandwidth.
00:48 Ben Carter: curious about fairshare. if we have emergency loads from hospitals, do we get priority?
00:56 Priya Nair: yes, you can configure routing policies. for example you can pin a project key to a dedicated pool and apply high priority, while noncritical traffic uses shared capacity.
01:25 [screen share noise]
01:40 Priya Nair: ok console home, projects on the left. here we create project keys under an org. org keys are umbrella keys, project keys are scoped - common pattern is to have an org key for billing and project keys per customer or environment.
02:05 Marta Ruiz: so project keys let us isolate usage per hospital?
02:12 Priya Nair: exactly. each hospital can be a project, with its own rate limits and quotas. you can also attach a routing policy to a key to pin to dedicated or region.
02:34 Lena Ortiz: what about audit logs and KMS? we need full immutability of logs and envelope encryption.
02:44 Priya Nair: we integrate with your KMS for model keys and support audit logs with S3 retention policies. logs include token level metadata and route decisions, we can redact pii fields on export.
03:10 Ben Carter: is there a neat way to limit token consumption per endpoint? some of our prompts vary wildly.
03:20 Jordan Liu: yes, quotas can be token-based or concurrency-based. you can set soft quotas to warn and hard quotas to block. also we have a per-route token limit so model configs can be safer.
03:45 Marta Ruiz: latency — if we pin to dedicated, what's typical p50 on gpus?
03:52 Priya Nair: depends on model and batch settings; for mid-size models with 2048 context we see 40-80ms p50 on A100 equivalent; P50 numbers in our catalog will be different for long sequences. for your 250ms SLA it's doable on dedicated.
04:18 Ben Carter: can routing fall back automatically if dedicated node is saturated?
04:24 Priya Nair: yes, policy-driven fallback. you can set fallback to compatible model variant in hosted region with lower priority and optional degradation controls.
04:45 Marta Ruiz: security question: do we need to open inbound for your control plane?
04:51 Jordan Liu: no, the private deployment options use customer VPC peering and our control plane can be whitelisted; for on-prem we provide an air-gapped package.
05:10 [laptop typing]
05:20 Priya Nair: now looking at rate limit policies. here is a token bucket config — you can set refill rate, burst size and scope it to org or project. we recommend small burst for patient-facing endpoints to keep latency predictable.
05:48 Ben Carter: example numbers?
05:52 Priya Nair: for example set refill 50 tokens/sec with burst 200 tokens for 1.5k token requests this means short spikes allowed but sustained load will be throttled.
06:15 Marta Ruiz: how do you monitor per-tenant token consumption?
06:20 Priya Nair: console has per-key dashboards; you can also stream events to your SIEM. we show token counts, latencies, and cost breakdown per key.
06:40 Ben Carter: about fairshare routing — can we implement weighted fairshare across projects in the same org?
06:47 Priya Nair: yes, we support weight-based shares and percent based. you can also reserve slices per project for guaranteed throughput.
07:05 Jordan Liu: quick note on billing: org keys are primary billing units; project keys roll up to orgs for invoices.
07:20 Marta Ruiz: what about sticky routing? if a long-running chat session lands on a node, we need to keep KV cache locality.
07:28 Priya Nair: great point — sticky routing pins session prefixes to cache-friendly nodes for the session lifetime. it's configurable by project.
07:50 Ben Carter: in POC we'd like to test burst traffic and failover. what's the recommended POC shape?
07:58 Priya Nair: we usually do traffic replay of real traces, a canary with 10% of traffic pinned to dedicated pool, and ramp to 100% while measuring p50/p95 and tail latencies.
08:18 Marta Ruiz: any specific limits on concurrency per key?
08:23 Priya Nair: yes concurrency quotas are per-key and can be hard capped. you can also reserve concurrency in Dedicated.
08:36 [slight crosstalk]
08:50 Lena Ortiz: compliance: SOC2 and ISO?
08:53 Jordan Liu: we are SOC2 Type II and working towards ISO; we'll share certs.
09:02 Marta Ruiz: do redwood logs include prompt text? we need to avoid storing PHI.
09:08 Priya Nair: logs can be configured to redact prompt text; we can stream hashed prompts instead or token counts only.
09:22 Ben Carter: what about per-tenant data retention?
09:26 Priya Nair: retention policies are per-org; you can set 30/90/365 days and export on-demand.
09:40 Jordan Liu: ok demo next section, rate policy templates.
10:00 Priya Nair: template: "clinical-low-latency" sets small batch size, dedicated pool, low token quota per request and higher priority. template can be applied to project keys.
10:20 Marta Ruiz: do you have any auto suggestions for batch sizes or quantization for cost reduction?
10:26 Priya Nair: Redwood Optimize suggests batching and quantization profiles based on historical token sizes. we can run suggestions against your traces during POC.
10:42 Ben Carter: can we set different SLOs per project? like hospital A needs 200ms, hospital B can accept 400ms.
10:49 Priya Nair: yes, SLOs are per-route and per-project. if SLO is missed we trigger regression alerts and optional automatic fallback.
11:10 Marta Ruiz: about encryption — envelope encryption with our HSM?
11:15 Priya Nair: yes we integrate with customer HSM for key wrapping and support KMS providers (AWS KMS, Azure, GCP).
11:30 Ben Carter: if a project exceeds its quota mid-session, does the request fail or queue?
11:36 Priya Nair: you can choose behavior: reject with 429, or queue briefly up to a configured window. for patient flows we recommend graceful degrade and fallback to cached responses for known scenarios.
12:05 [pause]
12:12 Jordan Liu: objections — cost is common. any concerns from you?
12:18 Marta Ruiz: main worry is cost creep with lots of small hospitals and variable prompts.
12:24 Jordan Liu: recommendation is project-level quotas and monitored soft alerts; Redwood Optimize will suggest where quant or batching can save 20-50% without quality loss.
12:40 Ben Carter: competitor question — what about Anthropic's platform?
12:44 Jordan Liu: similar offerings, but Redwood focuses on unified controls across hosted/dedicated/private deployments and stronger operational tooling for rollouts and routing.
13:05 Priya Nair: demo continues — API sample. here is curl to call with an org key, add X-Project-Key to route to project. show sample headers.
13:32 Ben Carter: do you recommend storing project keys in our vault?
13:36 Jordan Liu: yes, store keys in your vault and rotate regularly; console supports rotation and key expiry policies.
13:52 Marta Ruiz: what telemetry do you expose for debugging misrouted requests?
13:58 Priya Nair: tracing includes route decisions, reason codes for fallback, and model selection. traces are searchable by request id.
14:20 [background noise, slight transcription error: 'kv' became 'k v']
14:30 Ben Carter: how does KV cache behave across failovers?
14:36 Priya Nair: KV cache is sticky and we replicate short-lived prefixes; for full failover we warm cache with crossover heuristics but you may see cold-start tokens.
15:05 Marta Ruiz: PII — can you guarantee no PHI leaves our VPC?
15:10 Jordan Liu: with private deployment yes; for hosted we offer customer-managed encryption and strict retention; if absolute guarantee needed, on-prem is recommended.
15:30 Ben Carter: great. i want to map our internal tenants to project keys. any tooling?
15:36 Priya Nair: we have an import API and CSV upload to create projects in bulk and attach policies.
15:52 Marta Ruiz: ok show failure modes — what happens during capacity exhaustion?
15:58 Priya Nair: you'll see queued requests, then throttles per policy. if fallback policy is set, traffic moves to secondary pools. we emit alerts to channels defined in console.
16:20 Jordan Liu: let's talk about POC scope. propose 3-week POC: week 1 deploy keys and baseline traces, week 2 run traffic replay and measure, week 3 tune policies and handoff.
16:40 Marta Ruiz: timeline looks good. our compliance team needs SOC2 docs and network diagram.
16:46 Jordan Liu: will send that as part of next steps.
17:02 Ben Carter: question on billing granularity again — can we get per-project invoice lines?
17:08 Jordan Liu: yes, billing exports can break down by project and tag. we can also apply internal chargebacks.
17:25 Lena Ortiz: any pen-tests done on the control plane?
17:29 Jordan Liu: we do annual pen tests and can share redacted reports.
17:42 Priya Nair: quick show of Optimize suggestions - here it flagged routes with high token/response ratio and suggests 4-bit quantization for models used in non patient-sensitive flows.
18:05 Marta Ruiz: won't quantization affect output fidelity?
18:09 Priya Nair: for many tasks 4-bit quantization is transparent; for clinical reasoning we recommend evaluating on a prompt set — Optimize includes small eval harness.
18:30 Ben Carter: ok final Q: does Redwood offer joint-support during POC?
18:35 Jordan Liu: AE+SE support included, with optional dedicated success manager for enterprise POCs.
18:50 [logging start to wrap up]
19:05 Jordan Liu: recap — we'll send pricing, SOC2, network diagram, and POC runbook; Priya will prepare configs for project keys and a sample traffic replay; Marta will confirm stakeholders.
19:25 Marta Ruiz: thanks all, can we meet next Tuesday for kickoff?
19:30 Jordan Liu: i'll send a few slots, thanks everyone.
19:36 [end of recording - note: there are occasional word errors in transcription, e.g., 'k v' for KV.]
